_comment: Phase 71 example article — SUBSURFACE. The defining observable is LIGHT BLEEDING THROUGH: the stone glows softly where it is thin. Maps stay pale and low-contrast so the SCATTER is what you see, not the albedo. `subsurface_weight` must be nonzero — the master multiplies the scatter colour by it (default 0 = plain opaque stone). `subsurface_radius` is the length scale in cm; `_radius_scale` is the per-channel MFP (red travels furthest in stone, hence the warm falloff). Routes by the `marble` leaf-stem name exception (class stone -> Opaque otherwise). ** radius 0.6 -> 1.5 (71.12 smoke): the bleed was real but far too faint to read. The master approximates SSS as `SubsurfaceColor * saturate(RadiusScale * Radius) * Subsurface` -- UE legacy SSS has no mean-free-path input, so scatter MAGNITUDE is the only lever. At radius 0.6 that evaluated to ~(0.47,0.28,0.19): present, but a faint blush. At 1.5 the red channel saturates and it lands ~(0.78,0.70,0.47) -- visibly bleeding, warm falloff preserved. This is tuning the APPROXIMATION, not correcting a physical constant. Legacy SSS only really reads with light BEHIND the mesh. **
